subject: OPTIONS paragraph
notes: Rule: 'If any of the clauses are specified, then there shall be a terminating separator period.' cite.py --check 11.9.3 "If any of the clauses are specified, then there shall be a terminating separator period." -> OK  §11.9.3 1). CODE: `optionsParagraph : OPTIONS DOT (optionsClause+ DOT | DOT)? ;` - the first alternative is this rule (a written clause carries the terminating DOT, so a clause without the period cannot parse), the second is §11.9.2's independent `[.]` bracket written with no clause (`OPTIONS. .`, kb/Work PB1508), and omitting both is `OPTIONS.` alone. MEASURED: noperiod.cob (`OPTIONS.` + `DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION` with no period, then DATA DIVISION) is rejected at 2014 and 2023 with COBOL0307 "unexpected 'DATA'. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence." (the l1c20 negative); a clause with its period, `OPTIONS.` alone and `OPTIONS. .` compile and run at 2002/2014/2023 (the 2002 golden pb1508_options_period_bracket).
